newsitem.title: UK: Britain repays 4.4 billion stg debt in October.
newsitem.headline: Britain repays 4.4 billion stg debt in October.

text.p: Britain repaid 4.4 billion pounds ($7.33 billion) of public sector debt in October, reducing the government's borrowing requirement to 11.4 billion so far in the current financial year, official figures showed on Monday.
The repayment figure was higher than expected and government bond prices rose. Analysts said the figure gave a favourable backcloth ahead of the annual budget to be delivered on November 26.

Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke said the October figure showed the government was well on course to hit his forecast of 26.9 billion pounds of borrowing requirement in 1996-7. The switch from borrowing requirement to debt repayment was caused by large receipts of corporate tax in October.
"This is a very favourable figure. The backdrop for the chancellor going into the budget is very buoyant," said Peter Warburton of Robert Fleming.
